title: Concerning the Sun.

§ Concerning the Sun §
Once again, while the Apostle was sitting down in the gather-
ing of his disciples, at one moment the Sun shone forth, and he made fore-
most to proclaim to his disciples concerning the greatness of the Sun
and his godhood, saying: 'What is the manner in which they fashioned him to the like-
ness of the First Greatness, that which he was revealing to them?
For he is the gate of Life and the stronghold of
Peace, unto this great Aeon of the {5} {6}
⟨p.159⟩
But since Satan knows that he himself is the gate of the com-
ing-forth of the souls, he set forth a cutting-off of judgment
in his law, that 'No one shall worship him,' saying
that 'Whoever shall worship him, let him die,' so as also to call upon him,
(saying) that 'It is the Light who shall slay him.' He hindered the souls from
looking up themselves toward the Light. He commanded them to deny
the Light of their substance.
These men, then, are blind, with-
out (knowledge) in every matter; they have not known the Greatness of this Great Illuminator,
they have denied the manner of this great Light that shines forth upon them;
they have not perceived his greatness and his godhood;
n{0} either have they known the mercies that he does for them
today, while they yet stand fast in their body, at the time at which he
comes to th{1} cosmos and shines forth upon them, (saying) 'How many are the
agap{2} that he does for the men!' But they themselves deny
the {3}his manners, which they do not know, on all the days in which
this Great Illuminator shall shine forth his light. He does seven
good things for them, (yet) they do not see them.
{4} first good that he does for them is his light that
shines forth upon them, into the eyes of all men;
they see forth before them, walking in him, while he bears away from them
the blindness of their night which made them blind in its darkness.
{5} second is that, at the moment when he comes to the cosmos in his coming,
he brings rest and peace to the entire cosmos in his
coming. He himself takes away from them all fear, and the dis-
turbance with which their heart is filled because of all their night, for he
bea{6} the darkness of their midst by his light, and he drives forth
in this manner also draws (them) out of fear in his rest.
The third is his vigilance: since at the moment when he comes to the cos-
mos, all men indeed rise up — those who were sleeping —
and they awake. The wakeful ones, however, themselves cease their hand
{7}atching in fear, sitting before the encampments, while
{8} their watch of vigil because of his light that has shone forth
{9}osmos.
⟨p.160⟩
The fourth: that he nourishes and gives might and gives taste and scent
to the trees and the fruits and the crops and all the vegetables
and the flowers and the grass that is upon the whole earth.
The fifth: at the time when he shines in the whole cosmos,
the evil creeping things and the predatory wild beasts that are full of
evil are gathered into the lair, into their dens.
The sixth: at the time when his light shines, the plague
of men is at rest from the affliction; his light is poured
forth — dissolving the evil magics — from all the men of wickedness.
The seventh: that he is manifested forth and reveals forth from the
cosmos the sign of the Radiance of the aeons of the Light{0} which came
forth from there to this place — to (be) their sign in this cosmos — in order
that they may give light, that the entire creation may see — that for some {1} is the
vain-show which the doctrine of the Errant has set up: that not {2}
only have they not perceived the mystery of {3}
of this great Illuminator, but also all the other nourishings
that he does for them — they are forgetful of them, they do not perceive
them.
Thus indeed: as I have manifested to you concerning the sun
— that he is the doer of these seven goods in the cosmos — hear him
also, that I may teach you concerning the night — that she has wickednesses
all of them in her. Every time when the night shall come,
she does seven of evil in the cosmos.
The first of the wickednesses that the night does in the cosmos
is the Darkness which fills the entire cosmos with itself. For
at the time when the sun shall set forth from the cosmos and shall draw
unto himself his rays — at that very hour, the shadow
of the night spreads forth upon the entire cosmos; the eyes{4}
of men are filled with darkness; they cannot see forth, nor can they discern
with their eyes, because of the Darkness of the night which fills the
entire cosmos.
The second of the evil things that
the night does is her fear. For at the time when her
shadow is manifested forth, her fear and her disturbance{5}
upon all men; the entire cosmos is {6}
by the night.

The first is his light, because he gives-light through his light
to the cosmos and all the creatures that exist within it.
The second is his beauty, since at the time when he shines, he
habitually pours forth a beauty and an uprightness upon all creatures
and all things.
The third is the peace, because also at the time when the sun shall
shine upon the cosmos, all men are accustomed to receive a greeting
through it, and they give peace to one another.
The fourth is the life of the living soul, whom he habitually releases
out of all the fruits and the chains of heaven and earth.
The fifth: for he gives a power to the elements; he gives also a
scent and a taste to the whole Cross of Light. In this manner
you yourselves see, since his light gives-light
beyond all the lights that exist in the cosmos. {0}
His beauty also is beautiful beyond all the beauties of men. His peace
also is exalted beyond all powers and the {1} that
exist in the cosmos. His releasing — by which he releases
out of her, the living soul — is great in days, much more
than all releasings. The power that he gives to his
members is a great power, being mighty beyond all powers.
Once again, then, three further types are revealed in the sun for
the mystery of the first Greatness.
The first is the hiddenness of the disc of his stature, since
his stature, which has hidden itself at every season, does not diminish at
all — in the manner that the disc of the moon does not diminish [in] this {2}
at every moment when it is filled in him — to reveal the
mystery of the Father of the great Greatness, from whom all powers
and the gods come forth from him; he is not diminished ever,
neither does deficiency come to be in him at all.
The second: because his light is exalted beyond the light of
all the stars and all the lights that exist in the {3},
for the mystery of the light of the Father, because his {4} is
greatly exalted beyond the light of the {5}.
⟨p.163⟩
The third: that this sun is exalted, raised toward the upper place of
the All, exalted beyond the height of all the mountains and
the hills which exist upon the whole earth — corresponding to the mystery of
the Father of the Greatness: that he is exalted in the upper place over all the inhabitants
of his land of light. For the Father himself also
is exalted in the upper place over all the heights and the mountains of his
land of light. He is hidden in his icon at {0} season
and at every hour, from eternity unto eternity.

the sun, which is the second luminary — he who comes daily
into the cosmos to reveal {7} all of
his graces, to reveal upon him the sign concerning him
alone — that he is unburied: he is one out of the substance of the unburied
(one) who came forth from the unburied Father, having revealed himself in
the cosmos.
And the night, on her own part, being a sha-
dow, exists corresponding to the mystery of the darkness. Behold the myster-
y itself of her substance: they recognize him out of the cos-
mos through all the wickednesses. They recognize this myst-
ery daily in the cosmos. But the visions — they do not
{8} him in their wandering. They do not discriminate the myst-
{9} of the light and that of the darkness. Concerning this myst-
{10}, indeed, which is hidden from the visions, the Savior cast a sign
{11}, saying: 'Know that which is in the presence
{12}, and that which is hidden from you, indeed, shall be revealed to you.'
Once again the apostle said: 'You are sons of the day
{13} sons of the light. You are not sons
{14} sons of the darkness.'
⟨p.164⟩
But I am declaring to you, you my beloved — I am proclaiming them to your
souls — that you have recognized the mystery of the day and
(that) of the night, you have known that the day pertains to the myste-
-ry of the light, the night likewise (pertains) to the mystery of the dark-
ness — those that have not come forth out of one another. I am proclaiming them to
the one who has recognized the mystery, that he may discriminate the two sub-
stances — that of the Light and that of the Darkness — those that have not come
forth out of one another — that he may inherit the eternal Life.
